author: asukhobo
title: Debian Packages install fails — apt-get cannot connect to azure.archive.ubuntu.com
signature: Could not connect to azure.archive.ubuntu.com connection timed out|Network

failed_jobs.name: Debian Packages / Debian Packages
failed_jobs.symptom: apt-get install fails — connection timed out to azure.archive.ubuntu.com:80

key_errors: E: Failed to fetch http://azure.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/pool/main/g/glibc/libc-devtools_2.39-0ubuntu8.8_amd64.deb  Could not connect to azure.archive.ubuntu.com:80 (52.161.185.214), connection timed out [IP: 52.250.76.244 80]
E: Unable to fetch some archives, maybe run apt-get update or try with --fix-missing?
root_cause: The Debian Packages job failed during the 'Install debian packages & check conflicts' step because the GitHub Actions runner could not establish TCP connections to azure.archive.ubuntu.com:80. Multiple packages (libc-devtools, libgfortran5, libheif-plugin-aomenc, libhwloc15, libtbb12, and others) timed out after retries. This is a transient Azure CDN/network connectivity issue on the runner side — the PR changes (NPU model_hub_tests CI config) are unrelated to this failure.
reproduction_steps: N/A — transient runner network failure, not reproducible locally.
recommended_actions: Re-queue the PR or re-run the failed jobs — the failure is unrelated to the PR changes.
If the failure persists, check Azure status page for azure.archive.ubuntu.com CDN availability.
prevention_strategies: Consider adding apt retry settings (e.g., Acquire::Retries) or a fallback mirror in the debian packages workflow step to handle transient Azure CDN outages.
historical_context: First occurrence of this specific signature in the CI Doctor MQ database, but azure.archive.ubuntu.com connectivity timeouts are a known transient infrastructure pattern on Azure-hosted GitHub Actions runners.
